meta.name: Nikon D7200
meta.model: D7200 (Model Name: N1406) digital SLR camera
meta.summary: 24.2 MP Nikon DX-format digital SLR (EXPEED 4) with F mount, 51-point AF, dual SD slots, built-in flash and Wi-Fi/NFC. Geometry is scaled from D7200 photos to the 135.5 × 106.5 × 76 mm spec; service part numbers come from the D7100 parts list (shared chassis) and are marked where D7200 internals differ.

components.name: Rear cover unit
components.desc: Magnesium-alloy rear shell carrying the button column, multi selector and monitor opening (Fig.19).

components.name: Front cover unit
components.desc: Front shell around the lens mount; carries the Pv/Fn button rubbers (Fig.3).

components.name: Top cover unit
components.desc: Top shell incl. pentaprism housing; holds mode dial, top LCD, power switch and main/sub dials (Fig.14–18).

components.name: Bottom cover unit & tripod socket
components.desc: Base shell with 1/4 in. (ISO 1222) tripod socket; bottom plate unit carries the tripod boss (Fig.5, Fig.8).

components.name: Grip unit
components.desc: Rubber-covered right-hand grip shell around the battery chamber (Fig.2).

components.name: Connector covers (I/F cover unit)
components.desc: Left-side rubber covers over USB, external mic, HDMI (Type C), headphone and accessory terminal (Fig.2).

components.name: Memory card slot cover (SD lid)
components.desc: Right-side lid over dual SD/SDHC/SDXC (UHS-I) slots; card access lamp on rear (Fig.4).

components.name: Battery-chamber lid & base covers
components.desc: Battery lid with latch under the grip; MB-D15 contact cover and power connector cover (Fig.5–6).

components.name: Main chassis frame
components.desc: Internal body frame carrying boards, battery box and mirror box (Fig.7–8; no part number set).

components.name: Mirror box (front body unit)
components.desc: Front body/mirror box with mirror driving base and AF motor (Fig.9–11).

components.name: Lens mount (F bayonet)
components.desc: Nikon F bayonet with aperture coupling ring, lens contacts and lens release button (Fig.10).

components.name: Mirror unit
components.desc: Quick-return main mirror with sub-mirror to the AF module (Fig.9).

components.name: Shutter plate / focal-plane shutter
components.desc: Vertical-travel focal-plane shutter, 1/8000–30 s, X=1/250 s; shutter curtain is extremely thin (Fig.12).

components.name: Image sensor unit
components.desc: D7200: 23.5 × 15.6 mm CMOS, 24.2 MP effective (D7100: 24.1 MP — different sensor unit). Vibrates to shed dust.

parts.name: Image sensor unit (D7100 part — D7200 sensor differs)

components.name: AF sensor unit
components.desc: D7200: Multi-CAM 3500 II, 51 points (15 cross-type), –3 to +19 EV (D7100: –2 EV module).

parts.name: AF sensor unit (D7100 part — D7200 module differs)

components.name: Pentaprism & viewfinder optics
components.desc: Prism box with pentaprism, focusing screen, in-finder LCD and RGB metering sensor; ~100% coverage, 0.94× (Fig.13).

components.name: Viewfinder eyepiece, eyecup & diopter
components.desc: Eyepiece lens unit with diopter gear (–2 to +1 m⁻¹, eyepoint 19.5 mm) and DK-23 rubber eyecup.

components.name: Rear TFT monitor
components.desc: 3.2 in., approx. 1229k-dot TFT monitor (Fig.19).

components.name: Top control panel LCD
components.desc: Top monochrome LCD; D7200 adds an exposure meter indicator and refined lettering vs D7100.

components.name: Built-in flash
components.desc: Pop-up flash head, GN approx. 12 m (ISO 100), with flash PCB and main condenser (Fig.7, 17–18).

components.name: Accessory shoe
components.desc: ISO 518 hot-shoe with sync/data contacts and safety lock (Fig.16).

components.name: Mode dial & release mode dial
components.desc: Stacked mode dial (top, with lock release) and release mode dial S/CL/CH/Q/self-timer/MUP (Fig.15).

components.name: Shutter-release button & power switch
components.desc: Two-stage shutter-release inside the OFF/ON/illuminator power switch; movie-record, exposure-comp and metering buttons nearby (Fig.16).

components.name: Main command dial
components.desc: Rear thumb dial (Fig.17).

components.name: Sub-command dial
components.desc: Front finger dial on the grip (Fig.17).

components.name: Multi selector & rear-right controls
components.desc: Multi selector with OK and focus selector lock, AE-L/AF-L, live view selector/button, info button (Fig.19).

components.name: Rear-left button column
components.desc: Playback and delete above; MENU, WB/help/protect, QUAL/zoom-in, ISO/zoom-out and i buttons beside the monitor (Fig.19).

parts.name: Rear push button rubber (MENU, W/S, X/T, L/U, i)

components.name: Front buttons, AF-mode lever & IR window
components.desc: Pv and Fn buttons by the grip; flash, BKT, AF-M lever with AF-mode button and IR receiver window beside the mount (Fig.3, 6, 11).

parts.name: AF-M lever unit (focus-mode selector + AF-mode button)

components.name: AF-assist illuminator
components.desc: AF-assist (approx. 0.5–3 m), self-timer and red-eye lamp; may get hot with use (Fig.17).

components.name: Stereo microphone
components.desc: Built-in stereo microphone in front of the hot shoe (Fig.14).

components.name: Speaker
components.desc: Movie playback speaker, rear lower right (Fig.19).

components.name: EN-EL15 battery
components.desc: EN-EL15 Li-ion 7.0 V/1900 mAh (40 × 56 × 20.5 mm) in the grip; CIPA life approx. 1,110 shots on D7200 (950 on D7100).

components.name: Main boards & flex circuits
components.desc: Main PCB beside the SD slots, DC/DC and power-drive boards, I/F board. D7200 uses EXPEED 4 (D7100: EXPEED 3) so main boards differ.

parts.name: TOGO PCB unit (main board, D7100 part)

components.name: N-Mark (NFC) & Wi-Fi
components.desc: D7200-only built-in Wi-Fi (802.11b/g) and NFC; N-Mark on the left side. Not in the D7100 parts list.

components.name: Kit lens AF-S DX 18–105mm f/3.5–5.6G ED VR
components.desc: Type G zoom, approx. 76 mm dia × 89 mm from mount flange, 420 g, 67 mm filter.

faults.title: Lens aperture ring not at minimum
causes: CPU lens aperture ring not set to minimum aperture (highest f-number)
checks: Set the aperture ring to minimum aperture (highest f-number).
To use the ring for aperture, set Custom Setting f5 > Aperture setting to Aperture ring.

faults.title: Low battery
checks: Ready a fully-charged spare battery.

faults.title: Battery exhausted or cannot be used
causes: Extremely exhausted Li-ion or third-party battery in camera or MB-D15
checks: Recharge or replace the battery.
Use only Nikon-approved batteries.
If battery cannot be used, contact Nikon-authorized service.
faults.safety: Use only batteries approved for this equipment; do not expose to flame or heat.

faults.title: No lens / non-CPU lens without max aperture
faults.msg: Control panel: ΔF (aperture shown in stops from maximum)
causes: No lens attached, or non-CPU lens attached without specifying maximum aperture
checks: Specify maximum aperture with Non-CPU lens data in the setup menu; aperture value will then be displayed.

faults.title: No lens or non-CPU lens attached
causes: Non-CPU lens attached outside mode A or M
checks: Attach a non-IX NIKKOR lens; if a CPU lens is attached, remove and reattach it.
With a non-CPU lens, select mode A or M.

faults.title: Camera unable to focus
causes: Autofocus cannot focus on the subject
checks: Change composition or focus manually.

faults.title: Subject too bright — overexposure
faults.msg: Exposure indicators and shutter speed or aperture display flash
causes: Subject too bright for current settings
checks: Use a lower ISO sensitivity.
P: use a third-party ND filter; S: increase shutter speed; A: choose smaller aperture; effects mode: choose another shooting mode.

faults.title: Subject too dark — underexposure
faults.msg: Exposure indicators and shutter speed or aperture display flash
causes: Subject too dark for current settings
checks: Use a higher ISO sensitivity.
P: use flash; S: lower shutter speed; A: choose larger aperture.

faults.title: Bulb selected in mode S
causes: Bulb shutter speed selected in mode S
checks: Change shutter speed or select mode M.

faults.title: Time selected in mode S
causes: Time (--) shutter speed selected in mode S
checks: Change shutter speed or select mode M.

faults.title: Processing in progress
checks: Wait until processing is complete.

faults.title: Flash indicator flashes after firing
faults.msg: Viewfinder: flash indicator flashes for 3 s after flash fires
checks: Check photo in monitor; if underexposed, adjust settings and try again.

faults.title: Memory full / out of file numbers
causes: Memory insufficient to record further photos at current settings
Camera has run out of file or folder numbers
checks: Reduce image quality or size.
Delete photographs after copying important images to a computer.
Insert a new memory card.

faults.title: Camera malfunction
checks: Release shutter.
Consult a Nikon-authorized service representative if the problem persists or appears frequently.

faults.title: No memory card
checks: Turn camera off and confirm that card is correctly inserted (slide in until it clicks).
faults.safety: Turn camera off before inserting or removing cards.

faults.title: Memory card cannot be used
faults.msg: This memory card cannot be used. Card may be damaged. Insert another card. / Control panel: CArd, Err (flash)
checks: Use a Nikon-approved card.
Check that contacts are clean; if card is damaged, contact retailer or Nikon service.
Delete files or insert new card after copying important images.

faults.title: Camera cannot control Eye-Fi card
faults.msg: Monitor: Eye-Fi icon / Control panel: CArd, Err (flash)
causes: Camera can not control Eye-Fi card
checks: Check that Eye-Fi card firmware is up to date.
Copy files to a computer and format card, or insert new card.

faults.title: Memory card locked
faults.msg: Memory card is locked. Slide lock to “write” position. / Control panel: CArd, --- (flash)
checks: Slide card write-protect switch to “write” position.

faults.title: Eye-Fi card locked
faults.msg: Not available if Eye-Fi card is locked. / Control panel: CArd, Err (flash)
checks: Slide card write-protect switch to “write” position.

faults.title: Card not formatted
faults.msg: This card is not formatted. Format the card. / Control panel: [For] (flashes)
causes: Memory card not formatted for use in camera
checks: Format memory card (Setup menu > Format memory card, or hold O and Z buttons) or insert new card.
faults.safety: Formatting permanently deletes all data on the card.

faults.title: Clock has been reset
checks: Set camera clock (Setup menu > Time zone and date).

faults.title: Unable to start live view
faults.msg: Unable to start live view. Please wait.
causes: Internal temperature of the camera is high
checks: Wait for internal circuits to cool before resuming live view.

faults.title: Folder contains no images
causes: No images on card or in folder(s) selected for playback
checks: Select a folder containing images from Playback folder, or insert a card containing images.

faults.title: All images are hidden
causes: All photos in current folder are hidden
checks: Select another folder or use Hide image to allow at least one image to be displayed.

faults.title: Cannot display this file
causes: File created or modified on a computer or different camera
checks: File can not be played back on camera; view on a computer.

faults.title: Cannot select this file
causes: Selected image can not be retouched (created with another device)
checks: Choose an image created with this camera.

faults.title: Movie cannot be edited
checks: Only edit movies made with this camera that are at least two seconds long.

faults.title: Multiple smart devices connecting
faults.msg: Could not connect; multiple devices detected. Try again later.
causes: Multiple smart devices attempting to connect simultaneously
checks: Wait a few minutes before trying again.

faults.title: Wi-Fi error
checks: Select Disable for Wi-Fi > Network connection, then select Enable again.

faults.title: Network unavailable — camera hot
faults.msg: Network access not available until camera cools.
causes: Internal temperature of the camera is high
checks: Turn camera off and try again after waiting for camera to cool.

faults.title: Printer error
checks: Check printer; to resume select Continue (if available). See printer manual.

faults.title: Paper size mismatch
causes: Paper in printer is not of selected size
checks: Insert paper of correct size and select Continue.

faults.title: Paper jam
checks: Clear jam and select Continue.

faults.title: Out of paper
checks: Insert paper of selected size and select Continue.

faults.title: Ink error
checks: Check ink; to resume select Continue.

faults.title: Out of ink
checks: Replace ink and select Continue.

faults.title: CHARGE lamp flashes quickly
faults.msg: Charger CHARGE lamp flashes about eight times a second
checks: Confirm temperature is in range (charge indoors at 5–35 °C).
Unplug charger, remove and reinsert battery.
If problem persists, cease use and take battery and charger to retailer or Nikon service.
faults.safety: Cease use immediately if the fault persists.

faults.title: Low battery with mirror raised
faults.msg: Beep sounds and self-timer lamp flashes while mirror is locked up
causes: Battery running low during mirror lock-up for cleaning
checks: End cleaning or inspection immediately — shutter closes and mirror lowers after about two minutes.
faults.safety: Do not turn camera off or remove power while mirror is raised; the shutter curtain could be damaged.

faults.title: Camera on but does not respond
checks: Wait for recording to end.
Turn camera off; if it won't turn off, remove and reinsert battery or disconnect/reconnect AC adapter (data being recorded will be lost).

faults.title: Viewfinder out of focus
causes: Diopter not adjusted for user's eye
checks: Rotate diopter control until AF area brackets are sharp.
If needed: AF-S, single-point AF, center point, focus on a high-contrast subject, then adjust diopter.
Optional DK-20C corrective lenses.

faults.title: Viewfinder is dark
checks: Insert a fully-charged battery.

faults.title: Displays turn off without warning
causes: Short standby timer or monitor off delay
checks: Choose longer delays for Custom Setting c2 (Standby timer) or c4 (Monitor off delay).

faults.title: Control panel/viewfinder unresponsive and dim
causes: Display response and brightness vary with temperature
checks: Normal behavior; warm the camera.

faults.title: Fine lines around focus point / red display
causes: Normal for this type of viewfinder
checks: No action — not a malfunction.

faults.title: Camera takes time to turn on
causes: Many files or folders on card
checks: Delete files or folders.

faults.title: Shutter release disabled
causes: Memory card locked, full, or not inserted
f7 Slot empty release lock = Release locked with no card
CPU lens aperture ring not at highest f-number
Non-CPU lens attached outside mode A or M
Mode dial turned to S after bulb/time selected in M
checks: Check card is inserted, unlocked and has space.
Check Custom Setting f7.
Wait for flash to charge.
Focus or switch to manual focus.
Lock aperture ring at minimum or set f5 Aperture setting.
Select mode A or M for non-CPU lenses; choose a new shutter speed in S.

faults.title: Slow response to shutter-release
checks: Select Off for Custom Setting d4 (Exposure delay mode).

faults.title: No photo with ML-L3 remote
checks: Replace remote battery.
Choose an option other than Off for Remote control mode (ML-L3).
Wait for flash; reactivate remote mode; shade the IR receiver.

faults.title: Photos are out of focus
checks: Rotate focus-mode selector to AF.
Use manual focus or focus lock.

faults.title: Focus does not lock on half-press
causes: AF-C selected, or moving subject in AF-A
checks: Use AE-L/AF-L button to lock focus.

faults.title: Cannot select focus point
checks: Unlock focus selector lock.
Choose another AF-area mode.
Exit playback/menus.
Press shutter-release halfway to start standby timer.

faults.title: Cannot select AF mode / AF-area mode
checks: Set focus-mode selector to AF.

faults.title: Only one shot per press in continuous mode
checks: Continuous shooting is not available with built-in flash; lower the flash.

faults.title: Image size cannot be changed
checks: Select a JPEG image quality.

faults.title: Camera slow to record photos
checks: Turn long exposure NR off.

faults.title: AF-assist illuminator does not light
causes: AF-C mode or continuous-servo in AF-A
checks: Choose AF-S and center focus point.
Exit live view.
Set a9 to On.
Wait for illuminator to cool.

faults.title: Smudges appear in photographs
checks: Clean front and rear lens elements.
Perform image sensor cleaning.

faults.title: Noise (bright spots, fog, lines) in photos
causes: Some optional flashes at high ISO
checks: Lower ISO sensitivity.
Use Long exposure NR for exposures slower than 1 s.
Turn camera off and let it cool.
Set High ISO NR to High/Normal/Low.

faults.title: Flicker or banding in live view
causes: Flicker reduction does not match AC supply frequency
checks: Set Flicker reduction to match local AC frequency (Auto/50 Hz/60 Hz).

faults.title: Bright regions or bands in live view
causes: Flashing sign, flash or brief light source used during live view
checks: Avoid brief light sources during live view.

faults.title: No sound recorded with movies
causes: Microphone sensitivity set to Microphone off
checks: Change Microphone sensitivity in the movie shooting menu.

faults.title: Live view ends unexpectedly or will not start
causes: Extended live view or movie use
checks: Wait for internal circuits to cool and try again (camera may feel warm — not a malfunction).

faults.title: Image artifacts during live view
checks: Exit live view when camera is not in use.

faults.title: Menu item cannot be selected
causes: Option not available in current mode/settings or with no memory card
Battery info unavailable on AC adapter power
checks: Change mode or settings; insert a memory card.

faults.title: Full range of shutter speeds not available
checks: Set Custom Setting e1 Flash sync speed to 1/320 s (Auto FP) or 1/250 s (Auto FP) with compatible flash units.

faults.title: Colors are unnatural
causes: White balance does not match light source
checks: Adjust white balance.
Adjust Set Picture Control settings.

faults.title: Cannot measure white balance
causes: Subject too dark or too bright
checks: Use a correctly lit reference subject.

faults.title: Image cannot be preset WB source
checks: Use an image taken with this camera.

faults.title: White balance bracketing unavailable
checks: Select JPEG quality; end multiple exposure.

faults.title: Picture Control effects differ between images
causes: A (auto) selected for sharpening, clarity, contrast or saturation
checks: Choose a fixed setting for consistent results.

faults.title: Metering cannot be changed
checks: Release AE lock.

faults.title: Exposure compensation cannot be used
checks: Choose another mode.

faults.title: Reddish noise in long time-exposures
checks: Enable long exposure noise reduction.

faults.title: NEF (RAW) image not played back
checks: Only the JPEG copy is displayed; view RAW on computer.

faults.title: Pictures from other cameras not displayed correctly
causes: Recorded with other makes of camera
checks: View on a computer.

faults.title: Some images not displayed in playback
causes: Playback folder not set to All
checks: Select All for Playback folder.

faults.title: Portrait photos shown in landscape
causes: Auto image rotation off when shot
checks: Select On for Rotate tall.
Set Auto image rotation On.

faults.title: Cannot delete picture
checks: Remove protection.
Unlock card.

faults.title: Cannot retouch picture
causes: Photo cannot be further edited with this camera
checks: Edit on a computer.

faults.title: Cannot change print order
checks: Delete pictures; unlock card.

faults.title: Cannot select photo for printing
checks: Transfer to computer and print with Capture NX-D, or use NEF (RAW) processing to save as JPEG.

faults.title: Photo not displayed on HD video device
checks: Confirm that HDMI cable is connected.

faults.title: No response to HDMI-CEC TV remote
checks: Select On for HDMI > Device control in setup menu.
Adjust TV HDMI-CEC settings.

faults.title: Cannot transfer photos to computer
causes: OS not compatible with camera or transfer software
checks: Use a card reader to copy photos.

faults.title: Image Dust Off has no effect
causes: Dust reference data recorded before/after a different sensor cleaning
checks: Record new Dust Off reference data after each image sensor cleaning.

faults.title: Computer shows NEF images differently
causes: Third-party software ignores Picture Controls, Active D-Lighting, vignette control
checks: Use Capture NX-D.

faults.title: Smart device does not show camera SSID
checks: Select Enable for Wi-Fi > Network connection.
Turn smart device Wi-Fi off and on.

faults.title: Cannot connect using NFC
checks: Choose another connection method.

faults.title: Date of recording is not correct
causes: Camera clock less accurate than most clocks
checks: Check clock regularly and reset as necessary.

faults.title: Image sensor cleaning temporarily disabled
causes: Cleaning performed several times in succession (circuit protection)
checks: Wait a short time and try again.

sequence.name: Power on
sequence.desc: Rotate power switch to ON; control panel lights; image sensor vibrates to remove dust if Clean at startup is selected. First power-on shows language and clock setup.
hw: Startup cleaning skipped if flash is charging or controls are used

sequence.name: Half-press: meter and focus
sequence.desc: Pressing shutter-release halfway starts the standby timer, meters exposure and focuses (AF-S locks focus).
sequence.ends: In-focus indicator; focus locked in AF-S
hw: Focus point selectable only when standby timer is on

sequence.name: Shutter release
sequence.desc: Full press releases the shutter and records the image to the memory card; the memory card access lamp indicates card access.
hw: Release disabled: card locked/full/absent (f7), flash charging, not in focus, aperture ring not at minimum, non-CPU lens outside A/M

sequence.name: Live view
sequence.desc: Rotate live view selector to photo or movie and press the live view button; monitor shows the view through the lens with contrast-detect AF.
sequence.ends: Live view ends when exited, or automatically if internal temperature is high
hw: Live view ends automatically at high internal temperature

sequence.name: Movie recording
sequence.desc: In movie live view press movie-record button; records MOV H.264 with built-in or external stereo mic.

sequence.name: Image sensor cleaning (Clean now)
sequence.desc: Setup menu > Clean image sensor > Clean now; camera checks then vibrates sensor; busy indicator flashes.
hw: Do not remove power until cleaning ends

sequence.name: Lock mirror up for cleaning
sequence.desc: Setup menu > Lock mirror up for cleaning > Start; full press raises mirror and opens shutter to expose sensor.
sequence.ends: Turning camera off lowers mirror and closes shutter
hw: Only available above low battery level
Low battery: beep + self-timer lamp, shutter closes after ~2 min

sequence.name: Battery charging
sequence.desc: Insert EN-EL15 in MH-25a and plug in; CHARGE lamp flashes while charging; an exhausted battery fully charges in approx. 2 h 35 min.
hw: Will not charge below 0 °C or above 60 °C battery temperature

checks.name: Battery & card installation
checks.why: Correct installation avoids no-card and battery errors.
steps: Confirm power switch is OFF.
Insert battery, using it to hold the orange latch aside, until latch locks.
Insert one card in slot 1; slide in until it clicks.
Close covers.

checks.name: Charge EN-EL15 battery
checks.why: A fully-charged battery is required for normal use and for sensor cleaning.
steps: Insert battery in MH-25a and plug in.
CHARGE lamp flashes while charging; about 2 h 35 min from empty.
Charge indoors at 5–35 °C.
If CHARGE lamp flashes about 8×/s, check temperature, unplug, reinsert battery.

checks.name: Viewfinder diopter adjustment
steps: Rotate diopter adjustment control until AF area brackets are sharp.
Keep fingers/fingernails clear of your eye.

checks.name: Image sensor cleaning — Clean now
checks.why: Removes dust that shows as smudges.
steps: Hold camera base down.
Setup menu > Clean image sensor > Clean now > OK.
Do not remove power until setup menu returns.

checks.name: Set automatic sensor cleaning
checks.why: Keeps sensor clean at each power cycle.
steps: Setup menu > Clean image sensor > Clean at startup/shutdown.
Choose startup, shutdown, both, or off.

checks.name: Manual sensor inspection (blower only)
checks.why: For dust the vibration cleaning cannot remove. Nikon recommends service personnel do this.
steps: Insert fully-charged battery or AC adapter EH-5b + EP-5B.
Turn off and remove lens.
Turn on; Setup menu > Lock mirror up for cleaning > OK.
Press shutter-release fully to raise mirror.
Inspect sensor in light.
Remove dust with a blower only — no blower-brush; never touch or wipe the sensor.
Turn camera off; replace lens or body cap.

checks.name: Format memory card
checks.why: Clears For/card errors and prepares a card.
steps: Setup menu > Format memory card > choose slot > Yes, or hold O and Z buttons together then press again.
Back up images first — all data is deleted.
Do not turn off or remove battery/card while formatting.

checks.name: Two-button reset
checks.why: Restores default shooting settings when behavior seems wrong.
steps: Hold W (S) and E buttons (green dots) together for more than two seconds.
Control panel turns off briefly while settings reset.

checks.name: Clean body, lens, mirror and monitor
checks.why: Prevents dirt entering camera and image defects.
steps: Body: blower, then soft dry cloth; after beach use wipe with cloth lightly dampened in distilled water and dry.
Lens/mirror/viewfinder: blower; lens cleaner on soft cloth for fingerprints.
Monitor: blower, then soft cloth or chamois, no pressure.
No alcohol, thinner or volatile chemicals.
Never touch the shutter curtain.

checks.name: Long-term storage
checks.why: Prevents mold, battery leakage and damage.
steps: Remove battery, replace terminal cover, store cool and dry (15–25 °C).
Store camera dry and ventilated in a bag with desiccant; avoid >60% humidity, >50 °C or <–10 °C, mothballs, strong EM fields.
Monthly: turn camera on and release shutter a few times.
Every six months: run battery flat in camera before storing.

checks.name: Periodic inspection & service
steps: Have camera inspected by retailer or Nikon-authorized service every 1–2 years.
Have it serviced every 3–5 years (more often for professional use).
Include lenses and flash units.

defects.name: Dust smudges
defects.looks: Dark spots or smudges in the same place on every photo, most visible at small apertures.
isolate: Photograph a plain bright surface at a small aperture.
Swap lenses — if spots stay, it is the sensor.

causes.fix: Clean now; then manual blower cleaning or Nikon service
Clean lens with blower and lens cleaner
Change lenses away from dust; replace body cap promptly

defects.name: Noise / bright spots / fog
defects.looks: Randomly-spaced bright pixels, fog or lines, especially at high ISO or long exposures.
isolate: Compare low vs high ISO shots.

causes.fix: Lower ISO; set High ISO NR
Turn camera off and let it cool

defects.name: Out-of-focus photos
defects.looks: Subject is soft or the wrong area is sharp.
isolate: Check AF mode and focus point.

causes.fix: Use manual focus or focus lock

defects.name: Unnatural colors
defects.looks: Color cast or colors inconsistent between frames.
isolate: Check white balance setting vs light source.

causes.cause: White balance not matched to light

defects.name: Flicker / banding
defects.looks: Horizontal bands or flicker in live view or movies under artificial light.
isolate: Check lighting type and local AC frequency.

causes.fix: Set Flicker reduction to match AC frequency
Avoid brief light sources during live view

defects.name: Flash shadow / vignetting
defects.looks: Dark curved shadow at bottom of flash photos.
isolate: Check if a lens hood is fitted.

causes.fix: Remove lens hood when using built-in flash
Keep subject at least 0.6 m away
